record.paper_title: Some open problems in dynamical systems
record.original_question: Let f : R^{2n} → R^{2n} be a germ of a real-analytic symplectic diffeomorphism fixing 0, with linear part symplectically conjugate to r_{α_1} × ··· × r_{α_n}, where α = (α_1, ..., α_n) satisfies a Diophantine condition. Does every sufficiently small neighborhood of 0 contain a positive-Lebesgue-measure set of invariant Lagrangian tori for f?

evidence.quote: 3.4 - Conjecture. If f is real analytic, then f leaves invariant, in any small neighbourhood of 0, a set of positive Lebesgue measure of Lagrangian tori .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let n ≥ 1 and identify R^{2n} with the standard symplectic vector space. For α ∈ R, let r_α denote the planar rotation by angle 2πα, viewed as an element of Sp(2,R), and for a vector α = (α_1,…,α_n) ∈ R^n write r_α := r_{α_1} × ⋯ × r_{α_n} ∈ Sp(2n,R). Recall that α ∈ R^n is called Diophantine if there exist constants c > 0 and τ > 0 such that, for every k ∈ Z^n \ {0} and every m ∈ Z,
   |⟨k, α⟩ − m| ≥ c |k|^{−τ}.
A Lagrangian torus in R^{2n} is an embedded n-dimensional submanifold on which the standard symplectic form vanishes identically.

Let f : (R^{2n}, 0) → (R^{2n}, 0) be a germ of a real-analytic symplectic diffeomorphism fixing the origin, and assume that its linear part df(0) ∈ Sp(2n,R) is symplectically conjugate to r_α for some Diophantine vector α ∈ R^n.

Question: Does it follow that, for every sufficiently small neighborhood U of 0, the union of the f-invariant Lagrangian tori contained in U has positive Lebesgue measure?
artifact.status_search_result: This is a version of Herman's conjecture on accumulation of an elliptic Diophantine fixed point by Lagrangian invariant tori of positive measure. Eliasson, Fayad and Krikorian (2014) proved the conjecture under the additional assumption that the Birkhoff normal form at 0 satisfies a Rüssmann transversality condition, and showed unconditional accumulation by complex-analytic KAM tori; the fully degenerate (general) case in the form stated remains not definitively settled in the literature. Garay (2012) announced a positive resolution via KAM versal deformation theory, but this is not universally regarded as a complete proof of the original conjecture.

status_evidence.title: KAM-tori near an analytic elliptic fixed point (Eliasson–Fayad–Krikorian)
status_evidence.snippet: An elliptic fixed point with Diophantine frequency vector is always accumulated by invariant complex analytic KAM-tori; if the Birkhoff normal form satisfies a Rüssmann transversality condition, the fixed point is accumulated by real analytic KAM-tori that cover positive Lebesgue measure.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture is proved under a Rüssmann transversality condition on the Birkhoff normal form.

status_evidence.title: The Herman conjecture (Garay)
status_evidence.snippet: Herman conjectured the existence of a positive measure set of invariant tori at an elliptic Diophantine critical point of a Hamiltonian function. KAM versal deformation theory solves positively this conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: A claimed positive resolution exists, though it is not the consensus reference.
